title: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN MORALITY BECOMES PERSONAL PREFERENCE?
paragraphs: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN MORALITY BECOMES PERSONAL PREFERENCE?
Because nobody wanted to be the first person to say that something was wrong.
The conversation had drifted into familiar territory. Truth. Values. Ethics. Right and wrong.
"What's right for you isn't necessarily right for me."
And in that moment, a statement that sounds tolerant on the surface revealed one of the deepest spiritual crises of our generation.
Because once morality becomes personal preference, evil no longer needs permission to enter society.
Civilizations rarely collapse because they lose wealth.
They collapse because they lose truth.
History repeatedly shows that cultures die long before their buildings fall.
The biblical writers understood something modern humanity often forgets:
When people reject God as the source of moral authority, they do not eliminate morality.
They simply replace it with themselves.
The Book of Judges records one of the darkest periods in Israel's history with a chilling refrain:
"In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes." (Judges 21:25)
The Hebrew phrase is profoundly revealing.
What merely appeared right from personal perspective.
Modern culture often presents personal autonomy as the highest virtue.
Until we ask a dangerous question.
What if my heart is wrong?
The prophet Jeremiah delivered a warning that remains devastatingly relevant:
"The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?" (Jeremiah 17:9)
Scripture never teaches that human beings are incapable of good.
Human beings are capable of convincing themselves that evil is good.
Every atrocity ever committed was justified by someone who believed they were right.
The danger is not merely wicked people.
The danger is sincere people who have become their own moral authority.
The Apostle Paul described a future generation with unsettling precision:
"For the time is coming when people will not endure sound teaching..." (2 Timothy 4:3)
The Greek phrase for "sound teaching" is:
Truth that aligns humanity with reality.
Paul warned that people would accumulate teachers who tell them what they want to hear rather than what they need to hear.
Because preference became more attractive than truth.
The modern crisis is not an information problem.
People do not struggle because they cannot find truth.
People struggle because truth often demands surrender.
The Garden That Started It All
The battle over morality did not begin in modern universities.
The desire to define good and evil apart from God.
Every generation since has repeated the same rebellion.
Who gets to decide what is good?
Why Personal Preference Cannot Save Us
If morality is merely personal preference, then no one can meaningfully condemn injustice.
No one can say slavery is wrong.
No one can say exploitation is wrong.
No one can say genocide is wrong.
No one can say abuse is wrong.
At best, they can only say:
But human beings instinctively know something deeper.
We cry out against evil because we recognize objective moral reality.
We know some things are genuinely wrong.
C.S. Lewis famously observed that people appeal to moral standards precisely because they believe those standards exist beyond themselves.
It reflects the character of God.
Scripture never presents morality as a random list of divine commands.
God's commands flow from God's nature.
Because God is holy, holiness is good.
Because God is truthful, truthfulness is good.
Because God is loving, genuine love is good.
Because God is just, justice is good.
"God is light, and in him is no darkness at all." (1 John 1:5)
The Greek word for light is:
God is not merely someone who possesses truth.
He is the source from which truth flows.
Remove God from morality and truth becomes detached from its foundation.
Then power takes the place of preference.
Because when truth disappears, the strongest voices define reality.
The Lie That Feels Like Freedom
At first, moral autonomy feels liberating.
The pursuit of complete autonomy does not create freedom.
"Everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin." (John 8:34)
The human heart was never designed to function as its own ultimate authority.
When people reject God's rule, they do not become independent.
They simply become enslaved to other masters.
Christianity does not teach that morality is found by looking inward.
Christianity teaches that morality is found by looking upward.
And unlike every system built on self-justification, the Gospel begins with a startling confession:
None of us meet God's standard.
The Gospel does not flatter humanity.
"For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God."
The Greek word for sin is:
This is why Jesus Christ is not merely a moral teacher.
A teacher can explain the standard.
Only a Savior can carry us when we fail to meet it.
Our generation desperately needs more than new opinions.
The kind of truth that remains true whether people approve of it or not.
The kind of truth that existed before cultures were born and will remain after civilizations disappear.
"I am the way, and the truth, and the life." (John 14:6)
Notice He did not say He teaches truth.
What remains when every illusion falls apart.
The world is searching for authenticity.
And perhaps that is why moral confusion feels so exhausting.
The soul was never designed to carry the weight of being its own god.
It was created to know the One who already is.
Maybe the deepest question is not whether morality should be personal preference.
Maybe the deeper question is this:
How much pain have we created trying to replace God's voice with our own?
And perhaps even now, someone reading these words recognizes the exhaustion.
The burden of trying to define truth for yourself.
And redemption begins the moment we stop asking truth to submit to us and finally surrender ourselves to the Truth.
Be honest. This hit harder than you expected.
One day every opinion will fade, every trend will vanish, and every excuse will fall silent—but the truth of Christ will still be standing.
